definition: Water transferred from the land to the atmosphere through evaporation from soil and water, and transpiration from plants.
source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56: https://www.fao.org/4/X0490E/x0490e00.htm

definition: The difference between observed soil moisture and the long-term average for the same location and time of year.
source: NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive: https://smap.jpl.nasa.gov/

definition: The possibility that freezing temperatures will damage a crop. Risk depends on temperature, exposure, crop type, and growth stage.
An accounting of water entering, leaving, and being stored in a field, including precipitation, irrigation, evapotranspiration, runoff, and drainage.
A measure of accumulated warmth above a crop's base temperature, used to estimate plant development during a growing season.
A crop grown mainly to protect or improve soil between or alongside main crops, rather than to be harvested as the primary product.
source: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service: https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/

definition: The process by which certain microorganisms convert atmospheric nitrogen into forms plants can use. Many legumes support this process through root-associated bacteria.
source: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service: https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/
